newsitem.title: USA: Sears may test home improvement stores.
newsitem.headline: Sears may test home improvement stores.

text.p: Sears, Roebuck and Co said Friday it is considering testing a new free-standing store that would sell home decor and home refurbishment products.
The test would be the company's latest push into non-shopping-mall retailing, a market sector that it believes will boost its sales more quickly than mall-based stores.
"Sears is a growth company," said company spokesman Thomas Nicholson. "We are looking at all kinds of growth alternatives."
The Hoffman Estates, Illinois-based retailer could begin testing the concept with a few stores next year, Sears said. The company declined to provide further details about the new format.
Sears is the nation's largest home improvement retailer. It sells roofing, siding, windows and doors. It also sells home improvement products through licensed contractors who make house calls.
Sears operates 800 mall-based stores and about 1,500 free-standing outlets that sell furniture, hardware and auto products.
